conflicts.topic: Year of the Kangxi ban on writing the reign name
positions: 1677 (Kangxi 16): Bushell 1899 citing the Fuliang annals; Hobson 1915 citing Tao lu; Chinese journal abstract (中国陶瓷 2011); Chinese collector article naming magistrate 张齐仲.
1667: Burton & Hobson 1909; Christie's guide (2025) and Christie's specialist Kate Hunt as reprinted in Chinese (康熙六年).
conflicts.resolution: 1677 is better supported: it is the date given with the primary citation (Kangxi 16 in the Fuliang gazetteer via Tao lu), and Hobson himself moved from 1667 (1909) to 1677 (1915). 1667 looks like an error carried forward. Do not treat either date as a hard cut-off for empty rings.

positions: A local order of the Fuliang district magistrate Zhang Qizhong (Hobson 1915; Bushell 1899; Chinese article).

marks.description: The English word CHINA, stamped or printed, alone or with a Chinese mark.
marks.what_it_is: Export mark answering the US requirement (Tariff Act of 1890, sec. 6, in force 1 March 1891) that imports be marked in English with their country of origin.

periods.label: US marking rule
periods.note: used well into the 20th century

marks.dating_value: A genuine CHINA mark made for the US market is consistent with 1891 or later. It is not an upper limit: plain CHINA occurs on pieces from the 1960s–70s, especially for non-US markets. Absence of the mark proves nothing; not every import was marked, and marks could be on removable labels or only on packages (the statute also covered packages).
marks.later_copies: Plain CHINA appears on modern export ware; reign-type marks with CHINA are 20th century.
marks.notes: Statute: 'articles of foreign manufacture, such as are usually or ordinarily marked… and all packages… shall… be plainly marked… in legible English words, so as to indicate the country of their origin' (paraphrase). Gotheborg once attributes the rule to a 'U.S. Stamp Act of 1894'; the statute text shows the 1890 Act, effective 1 March 1891.

marks.dating_value: Each cyclical year recurs every 60 years, so without a reign title or other evidence a cyclical date fits several years (e.g. 甲子 = 1864, 1924, 1984). Use style and other marks to choose; Gotheborg finds such dates on late-19th to mid-20th c. porcelain often correct once the cycle is fixed.
marks.later_copies: Cyclical dates continue on modern porcelain.
marks.notes: Pointer only; see the ganzhi converter.

facts.claim: The cycle has 60 terms and repeats; it cannot fix a year without other information
